ELIGULI HAN

New York University · Mathematics & Computer Science Undergraduate

New York, NY hh3494@nyu.edu github.com/Eliguli712 LinkedIn

Mathematics and computer science undergraduate developing computational approaches to animal anatomy, acoustics and environmental perception. Research interests include fossil cetacean cranial anatomy, temnospondyl biomechanics, and the connection between three-dimensional geometry and biological function.

Current research reportTooth-scale Stress Localisation in a µCT-derived Otodus megalodon ModelWork in progress · 12 pages · 25 November 2026

Han, E. (2026). Tooth-scale Stress Localisation in a μCT-derived Otodus megalodon Model: Calibrated Geometry, Numerical Verification and Regional Sensitivity.

Work in progress · 12 pages · 25 November 2026

Calibrated CT geometry, regional stress quantiles, and same-domain P1/P2 verification. Twelve fitted tooth–jaw finite-element cases test how attachment stiffness and loading direction redistribute principal tensile stress at the cutting margins. Includes native-surface figures, material and attachment sensitivity, and links to public geometry and numerical data.

Special Projects / Sonderprojekte

VRONTIKI SYNAISTHESMA · PUBLIC DIGITAL MUSEUM

Cenozoic Chronicle

Evolution × Civilisation · 160 160 · English / Deutsch

A double chronology linking 160 evolutionary events with 160 historical events, from the Paleocene to the Miocene. A fixed scale of 10,000 geological years per narrative year supports an order-preserving timeline, civilisation motifs and four comparison curves. The evolution workspace traces 8 comparative sequences, 51 anatomical profiles and 20 calibrated feature axes, with editable inference branches and source-linked evidence.

Eine doppelte Chronologie verbindet 160 Evolutionsereignisse mit 160 historischen Ereignissen vom Paläozän bis zum Miozän. Der feste Maßstab von 10.000 geologischen Jahren pro Erzähljahr trägt eine reihenfolgetreue Zeittafel, Zivilisationsmotive und vier Vergleichskurven. Der Evolutionsraum erschließt 8 Vergleichsfolgen, 51 anatomische Profile und 20 kalibrierte Merkmalsachsen mit bearbeitbaren Inferenzzweigen und verknüpfter Evidenz.

Selected Research & Computational Projects

Live Orca · Skeletal Anatomy & Measured Movement

Ongoing

Interactive natural-history exhibit · Orcinus orca, MSNUP C–301 · JavaScript, WebGL, Python

  • Preserves all 2,486,130 original scan triangles and provides a 99,982,422-cell surface-derived occupancy field, anatomical region isolation, editable pose and downloadable source geometry.
  • Replays 58,291 calibrated DTAG samples at 50 Hz from Tennessen, Holt & Wright (2024), including measured pitch, roll, heading and depth. Local vertebral motion is identified separately as a reconstruction.
  • Extracts localized visible crown, alveolar-margin and surface-depression candidates from the native scan, transfers shared evidence across display resolutions, and offers learned display stabilization with direct comparison to the original movement record.

Explore the skeleton and movement record · Original movement dataset

Antiterrastrae · Volumetric Biosonar & Scientific Visualization

Ongoing

Self-directed computational prototype · JavaScript, HTML/CSS, WebGL

  • Developing an interactive aquatic simulation connecting three-dimensional animal surface geometry with acoustic propagation, echoes, and temperature-, salinity- and depth-dependent environmental structure.
  • Implemented a tetrahedral finite-element module for scalar acoustic eigenmodes, Kp = λMp, with stiffness and consistent mass matrices, Cholesky transformation and Jacobi eigenvalue iteration.
  • Integrated WebGL echo rendering with a Canvas fallback, adjustable acoustic parameters, and VTK/OBJ export of surface and volumetric geometry for inspection and further analysis.

Cynthiacetus peruvianus · Digital Cranial Anatomy

Ongoing

Independent project in development · MNHN holotype MNHN.F.PRU10

  • Initiated data-access correspondence with Guillaume Billet at the Muséum national d’Histoire naturelle; availability of cranial and mandibular surface scans was confirmed, subject to a formal collections request and use conditions.
  • Developing a staged research plan linking surface morphology to CT/μCT segmentation, virtual endocast reconstruction and exploratory cranial biomechanics, according to available data and documented anatomical assumptions.

Marine Mammal Field Observation & Research — Opportunities Sought

Cetacean Field Ecology, Coastal Surveys & Photo-Identification

Winter / Spring / Summer 2027

Prospective supervised field research · Atlantic Marine Conservation Society (AMSEAS) inquiry

  • Seeking vessel- and shore-based marine mammal surveys, pinniped population documentation, coastal monitoring patrols, systematic observation records and individual photo-identification.
